# Provider Selection — Final Decision

## Decision

The Atlas Lantern team selected Aster A as the approved model provider for the
synthetic pilot and its next integration slice. The selection is an approved
decision, while regional readiness actions remain tracked separately.

## Rejected Alternatives

Borealis B was rejected because the residency exception and additional
operational burden were not acceptable for this slice. Cedar C was rejected
because the review did not establish an auditable region commitment and its
streaming behavior did not meet the adapter requirement.

## Rationale

The decision prioritizes an auditable data boundary and an owned operational
path over the faster early prototype. The office-hours prototype observation
does not supersede this record.

## Approval

The decision was approved on 2026-01-22 by the Atlas Lantern technical review
group. Remaining readiness work must not be described as completed adoption.

# Provider Comparison Review

## Comparison

The review compared Borealis B, Aster A, and Cedar C against the Atlas Lantern
pilot requirements. Prototype response quality was not treated as sufficient
for adoption.

## Data Residency

Aster A documented processing in the synthetic `eu-north` region used by the
pilot. Borealis B required a residency exception, and Cedar C did not provide
an auditable region commitment in the review packet.

## Operations

Aster A had a named operational escalation path and a bounded usage report.
Borealis B would have required the small team to own an additional failover
runbook. Cedar C lacked the streaming behavior required by the adapter.

## Recommendation

The review recommended Aster A for the pilot, subject to regional evidence and
an on-call runbook. Borealis B and Cedar C remained comparison candidates until
the approval record was written.

date: 2026-02-14
status: approved
authority: decision_record
---
# Retrieval Upgrade — Final Decision

## Decision

The team approved a phased hybrid retrieval path: retain BM25 as the lexical
baseline and add semantic retrieval behind the measured rollout boundary.

## Rejected Alternative

Replacing BM25 with pure semantic retrieval was rejected for the first release.
The benchmark showed lower recall on the reviewed sample and the team would
lose a useful exact-term diagnostic baseline.

## Rollout Boundary

This decision approves the approach, not unrestricted rollout. Embedding cache
security and release-readiness actions remain open.

## Approval

The retrieval review group approved this decision on 2026-02-14. A later status
update is authoritative for action completion.

metadata.title: 01-semantic-draft
metadata.content:
---
date: 2026-02-03
status: superseded
authority: working_draft
---
# Retrieval Upgrade — Semantic Draft

## Problem

Exact-term queries were missing a few paraphrases in the Atlas Lantern search
sample. The draft proposed replacing the existing BM25 baseline with a pure
semantic index.

## Proposed Change

The draft proposed removing BM25 from the first release and routing every query
through embeddings. It treated the early synonym-query prototype as evidence
that the lexical path was no longer needed.

## Open Risks

The draft had not measured cache isolation or whether exact-term diagnostics
would remain available. It was superseded after the benchmark review.

## Supersession

The February 3 pure-semantic proposal was superseded by the February 14
approved phased-hybrid decision. It is retained only as historical proposal
evidence and is not the current retrieval policy.

metadata.title: 02-benchmark-review
metadata.content:
---
date: 2026-02-10
status: reviewed
authority: benchmark_review
---
# Retrieval Upgrade — Benchmark Review

## Benchmark Scope

The synthetic benchmark compared the existing BM25 baseline, a pure semantic
replacement, and a phased hybrid design across exact terms and paraphrases.

## Results

The phased hybrid design reached 0.92 recall on the reviewed sample. Pure
semantic replacement reached 0.84, while the BM25 baseline remained useful for
exact-term diagnostics and reproducible failure analysis.

## Recommendation

The review recommended keeping BM25 as the lexical baseline and introducing
semantic retrieval in a phased hybrid path. The result does not authorize a
production release by itself.

## Risks

Embedding cache isolation and retention still required a security review. The
review did not claim that the cache action was complete.

metadata.content:

status: in_progress
authority: status_update

# Retrieval Upgrade — Cache Security Status

## Current Status

The BM25 baseline check is completed and the hybrid pilot is in progress. The
approved phased approach has not been changed.

## Blocked Action

Yuan Li owns the embedding-cache security review, due 2026-02-28. It is
blocked because isolation and retention controls have not received security
sign-off.

## Completed Work

The team recorded the baseline benchmark and a reversible local cache fixture.
This is not evidence that a production cache is approved.

# Retrieval Upgrade — Release Readiness

## Current Status

The approved target remains phased hybrid retrieval with BM25 retained. The
hybrid pilot has not crossed the release boundary.

## Release Blocker

Release is blocked until the embedding-cache security review is signed off.

## Evidence Boundary

The benchmark and local fixture support the design decision. They do not prove
that the production cache or semantic rollout is complete.

metadata.content:
---
date: 2026-03-03
status: open
authority: incident_intake
---
# Deployment Incident — Intake

## Impact

The Atlas Lantern synthetic service recorded 18 timeout/replay events during a
staging-to-canary exercise. A few action requests were observed twice; the
initial intake did not establish whether the provider or the replay path was
responsible.

## Initial Hypothesis

The first hypothesis was provider latency. It was recorded for investigation,
not as a confirmed root cause.

## Investigation Status

The incident review was still open on 2026-03-03. The root-cause review and
mitigation decision are later, more authoritative records.

metadata.title: 02-root-cause-review
metadata.content:
---
date: 2026-03-04
status: reviewed
authority: incident_review
---
# Deployment Incident — Root Cause Review

## Root Cause

The timeout recovery path replayed a request without carrying its idempotency
key. The replay therefore passed the duplicate guard as a new request and could
produce a duplicate action. Provider latency contributed to the timeout but
was not the primary root cause.

## Evidence

The review matched the duplicate actions to requests whose original attempt
had a key but whose recovery attempt did not. The trace comparison was completed
for the synthetic incident sample.

## Containment

The review recommended a bounded replay guard and end-to-end idempotency-key
propagation. Production verification was left to the status update.

metadata.title: 05-postmortem-draft
metadata.content:
---
date: 2026-03-03
status: superseded
authority: working_draft
---
# Deployment Incident — Postmortem Draft

## Draft Summary

The first postmortem draft used the phrase “mitigation complete” after a local
guard test. That phrase was a planning shorthand and was not verified against
the later staging, canary, and production status.

## Hypothesis

The draft attributed the incident mainly to provider timeout behavior. The
review later identified the missing idempotency key on replay as the primary
cause.

## Supersession

This draft was superseded by the root-cause review and the remediation status
update. It cannot establish production completion.

metadata.title: 03-mitigation-decision
metadata.content:
---
date: 2026-03-05
status: approved
authority: decision_record
---
# Deployment Incident — Mitigation Decision

## Decision

The team approved propagating an idempotency key through the timeout recovery
path and adding a bounded replay guard. This is the selected mitigation for the
synthetic service.

## Rejected Alternative

An active-active deployment was rejected for this incident slice. It would add
another route for duplicated side effects and operational coordination before
the idempotency defect was fixed.

## Verification Boundary

The decision record approves the mitigation design. It does not claim that the
production rollout or load-test verification is complete.

## Approval

The incident review group approved this mitigation on 2026-03-05.

metadata.title: 06-operations-office-hours
metadata.content:
---
date: 2026-03-09
status: informational
authority: discussion_note
---
# Deployment Incident — Operations Office Hours

## Observation

One participant said an active-active topology could avoid a single queue. The
comment was an exploratory operations observation, not an incident decision.

## Decision Boundary

No deployment change was approved in this discussion. The approved mitigation
is recorded in the incident decision note.

## Follow-up

The facilitator suggested documenting queue ownership after the replay runbook
review. No owner or completion date was assigned here.

metadata.content:

date: 2026-03-08
status: partial
authority: status_update
---

## Current Status

The idempotency guard was deployed to staging and exercised in canary. End-to-
end production verification remains partial; the status update does not mark
the mitigation fully complete.

## Open Actions

- Inez Park owns the replay runbook, due 2026-03-12; the action is blocked on
  an operations review.
- Tao Lin owns the duplicate-event dashboard query; it is in progress.
- The production load test has no assigned owner and remains pending.

## Completion Meaning

Staging deployment and canary exercise are completed checkpoints. They must not
be reported as production verification or as proof that all remediation work is
finished.

# Deployment Incident — Intake

## Impact

The Atlas Lantern synthetic service recorded 18 timeout/replay events during a
staging-to-canary exercise. A few action requests were observed twice; the
initial intake did not establish whether the provider or the replay path was
responsible.

## Initial Hypothesis

The first hypothesis was provider latency. It was recorded for investigation,
not as a confirmed root cause.

## Investigation Status

The incident review was still open on 2026-03-03. The root-cause review and
mitigation decision are later, more authoritative records.

metadata.content:

# Deployment Incident — Postmortem Draft

## Draft Summary

The first postmortem draft used the phrase “mitigation complete” after a local
guard test. That phrase was a planning shorthand and was not verified against
the later staging, canary, and production status.

## Hypothesis

The draft attributed the incident mainly to provider timeout behavior. The
review later identified the missing idempotency key on replay as the primary
cause.

## Supersession

This draft was superseded by the root-cause review and the remediation status
update. It cannot establish production completion.

metadata.title: 02-root-cause-review
metadata.content:
---
date: 2026-03-04
status: reviewed
authority: incident_review
---
# Deployment Incident — Root Cause Review

## Root Cause

The timeout recovery path replayed a request without carrying its idempotency
key. The replay therefore passed the duplicate guard as a new request and could
produce a duplicate action. Provider latency contributed to the timeout but
was not the primary root cause.

## Evidence

The review matched the duplicate actions to requests whose original attempt
had a key but whose recovery attempt did not. The trace comparison was completed
for the synthetic incident sample.

## Containment

The review recommended a bounded replay guard and end-to-end idempotency-key
propagation. Production verification was left to the status update.

metadata.title: 03-mitigation-decision
metadata.content:
---
date: 2026-03-05
status: approved
authority: decision_record
---
# Deployment Incident — Mitigation Decision

## Decision

The team approved propagating an idempotency key through the timeout recovery
path and adding a bounded replay guard. This is the selected mitigation for the
synthetic service.

## Rejected Alternative

An active-active deployment was rejected for this incident slice. It would add
another route for duplicated side effects and operational coordination before
the idempotency defect was fixed.

## Verification Boundary

The decision record approves the mitigation design. It does not claim that the
production rollout or load-test verification is complete.

## Approval

The incident review group approved this mitigation on 2026-03-05.

The evaluation rollout will gate release on deterministic metrics for decision
accuracy, rejected-alternative accuracy, unresolved-item recall, and evidence
validity. LLM-judge output is diagnostic only and must not gate release.

The first rollout covers the synthetic decision, rejection, unresolved-item,
and evidence cases. A multilingual slice is tracked separately and is not
silently treated as complete.

The proposed 0.80 next-action threshold was not approved in this decision. It
requires a later sign-off before it can become a release rule.

## Approval

The evaluation group approved this boundary on 2026-03-21.

# Agent Evaluation — Metric Design Review

## Deterministic Metrics

Decision accuracy, rejected-alternative accuracy, unresolved-item recall, and
evidence validity can be checked against the frozen synthetic Gold records.
These metrics are reproducible enough to gate the first rollout.

## Judge Boundary

An LLM judge may provide diagnostic comments, but judge output is too variable
to serve as the release gate for this slice. Judge results must remain separate
from deterministic metrics.

The draft's 0.80 next-action threshold still required an explicit approval
decision. This review did not assign an owner or approve the threshold.

## Recommendation

Use deterministic metrics for release gating and keep judge feedback
diagnostic until a later review supplies reproducibility evidence.

# Internal Tool Integration — Security Review

## Boundary Finding

A write-enabled direct API is not allowed in the first read-only integration
path because its permission and audit boundary is too broad for the slice.

## Approved Candidate

The review approved evaluating a read-only connector together with an export
bundle. Both paths must expose source references and retain an audit-friendly
checksum; neither path may mutate the source system.

## Remaining Review

The connector read permission was verified in the synthetic environment. Export
retention and checksum ownership remained open for the integration decision.

metadata.title: 05-sandbox-demo
metadata.content:
---
date: 2026-04-16
status: informational
authority: discussion_note
---
# Internal Tool Integration — Sandbox Demonstration

## Observation

An isolated sandbox demonstration showed that the direct API could write a
sample record. The demonstration was used to expose the permission risk and
was not an approved integration path.

## Decision Boundary

No source record was changed by the synthetic review corpus. The approved

metadata.content:
---
date: 2026-01-18
status: approved
authority: decision_record
---
# Data Retention — Final Policy Decision

## Decision

The approved current policy retains active records for 180 days and archived
records for 365 days. The policy distinguishes the two classes rather than
using one uniform period.

## Rejected Alternative

The uniform 90-day deletion proposal was rejected because it would remove audit
history too early and would not preserve the archive class.

## Legal Boundary

Deletion exceptions still require legal sign-off. The policy decision does not
authorize a deletion job to run before that sign-off.

## Approval

The compliance review group approved this policy on 2026-01-18.

metadata.title: 02-retention-review
metadata.content:
---
date: 2026-01-12
status: reviewed
authority: compliance_review
---
# Data Retention — Policy Review

## Review Finding

Uniform 90-day deletion would remove audit history too early and would not
distinguish active working records from archived records.

## Recommendation

The review recommended 180 days for active records and 365 days for archived
records. Deletion exceptions require a separate legal sign-off.

## Migration Constraint

Mapping and dry-run work may proceed, but no record deletion is authorized
until the legal sign-off and exception list are complete.

# Provider Selection — Early Proposal

## Context

The Atlas Lantern team needed a hosted model for a synthetic document-review
pilot. The first comparison was made before the regional data boundary and
on-call ownership were written down.

## Candidate View

Borealis B was the early favorite because its prototype returned structured
JSON quickly and required little adapter code. This note records a proposal,
not an adoption decision.

## Open Questions

The team still needed evidence about data residency, operational ownership,
and the cost of keeping a fallback provider. The proposal was superseded by a
later comparison review.

metadata.title: 03-final-decision
metadata.content:
---
date: 2026-01-22
status: approved
authority: decision_record
---
# Provider Selection — Final Decision

## Decision

The Atlas Lantern team selected Aster A as the approved model provider for the
synthetic pilot and its next integration slice. The selection is an approved
decision, while regional readiness actions remain tracked separately.

## Rejected Alternatives

Borealis B was rejected because the residency exception and additional
operational burden were not acceptable for this slice. Cedar C was rejected
because the review did not establish an auditable region commitment and its
streaming behavior did not meet the adapter requirement.

## Rationale

The decision prioritizes an auditable data boundary and an owned operational
path over the faster early prototype. The office-hours prototype observation
does not supersede this record.

## Approval

The decision was approved on 2026-01-22 by the Atlas Lantern technical review
group. Remaining readiness work must not be described as completed adoption.

# Provider Adoption — Readiness Snapshot

## Current Status

Aster A remains the approved provider for the Atlas Lantern slice. The local
adapter check is complete, but regional readiness is not closed.

## Remaining Gates

Regional evidence validation is blocked pending legal confirmation. The
on-call runbook is still in progress. These gates are prerequisites for the
regional pilot and are not evidence that Borealis B was adopted.

## Ownership

Chen Rui is the proposed owner for the regional evidence follow-up, but the
status update does not assign a replacement owner. Omar Wu remains responsible
for finishing the on-call runbook.

metadata.title: 02-comparison-review
metadata.content:
---
date: 2026-01-15
status: reviewed
authority: technical_review
---
# Provider Comparison Review

## Comparison

The review compared Borealis B, Aster A, and Cedar C against the Atlas Lantern
pilot requirements. Prototype response quality was not treated as sufficient
for adoption.

## Data Residency

Aster A documented processing in the synthetic `eu-north` region used by the
pilot. Borealis B required a residency exception, and Cedar C did not provide
an auditable region commitment in the review packet.

## Operations

Aster A had a named operational escalation path and a bounded usage report.
Borealis B would have required the small team to own an additional failover
runbook. Cedar C lacked the streaming behavior required by the adapter.

## Recommendation

The review recommended Aster A for the pilot, subject to regional evidence and
an on-call runbook. Borealis B and Cedar C remained comparison candidates until
the approval record was written.

metadata.content:
---
date: 2026-03-04
status: reviewed
authority: incident_review
---
# Deployment Incident — Root Cause Review

## Root Cause

The timeout recovery path replayed a request without carrying its idempotency
key. The replay therefore passed the duplicate guard as a new request and could
produce a duplicate action. Provider latency contributed to the timeout but
was not the primary root cause.

## Evidence

The review matched the duplicate actions to requests whose original attempt
had a key but whose recovery attempt did not. The trace comparison was completed
for the synthetic incident sample.

## Containment

The review recommended a bounded replay guard and end-to-end idempotency-key
propagation. Production verification was left to the status update.

metadata.title: 01-incident-intake
metadata.content:
---
date: 2026-03-03
status: open
authority: incident_intake
---
# Deployment Incident — Intake

## Impact

The Atlas Lantern synthetic service recorded 18 timeout/replay events during a
staging-to-canary exercise. A few action requests were observed twice; the
initial intake did not establish whether the provider or the replay path was
responsible.

## Initial Hypothesis

The first hypothesis was provider latency. It was recorded for investigation,
not as a confirmed root cause.

## Investigation Status

The incident review was still open on 2026-03-03. The root-cause review and
mitigation decision are later, more authoritative records.

metadata.title: 05-postmortem-draft
metadata.content:
---
date: 2026-03-03
status: superseded
authority: working_draft
---
# Deployment Incident — Postmortem Draft

## Draft Summary

The first postmortem draft used the phrase “mitigation complete” after a local
guard test. That phrase was a planning shorthand and was not verified against
the later staging, canary, and production status.

## Hypothesis

The draft attributed the incident mainly to provider timeout behavior. The
review later identified the missing idempotency key on replay as the primary
cause.

## Supersession

This draft was superseded by the root-cause review and the remediation status
update. It cannot establish production completion.

metadata.title: 03-mitigation-decision
metadata.content:
---
date: 2026-03-05
status: approved
authority: decision_record
---
# Deployment Incident — Mitigation Decision

## Decision

The team approved propagating an idempotency key through the timeout recovery
path and adding a bounded replay guard. This is the selected mitigation for the
synthetic service.

## Rejected Alternative

An active-active deployment was rejected for this incident slice. It would add
another route for duplicated side effects and operational coordination before
the idempotency defect was fixed.

## Verification Boundary

The decision record approves the mitigation design. It does not claim that the
production rollout or load-test verification is complete.

## Approval

The incident review group approved this mitigation on 2026-03-05.

# Agent Evaluation — Rollout Decision

## Decision

The evaluation rollout will gate release on deterministic metrics for decision
accuracy, rejected-alternative accuracy, unresolved-item recall, and evidence
validity. LLM-judge output is diagnostic only and must not gate release.

## Scope

The first rollout covers the synthetic decision, rejection, unresolved-item,
and evidence cases. A multilingual slice is tracked separately and is not
silently treated as complete.

## Unapproved Threshold

The proposed 0.80 next-action threshold was not approved in this decision. It
requires a later sign-off before it can become a release rule.

## Approval

The evaluation group approved this boundary on 2026-03-21.

# Agent Evaluation — Initial Proposal

## Proposal

The draft proposed using an LLM judge as a release gate and suggested a
next-action score threshold of 0.80. These were planning ideas, not approved
release rules.

## Rationale

The author expected a judge to capture helpfulness that exact deterministic
checks might miss. No reproducibility study or owner assignment was attached.

## Open Questions

variance would be handled, and whether the next-action threshold had an
approver.

status: reviewed
authority: metric_review
---
# Agent Evaluation — Metric Design Review

## Deterministic Metrics

Decision accuracy, rejected-alternative accuracy, unresolved-item recall, and
evidence validity can be checked against the frozen synthetic Gold records.
These metrics are reproducible enough to gate the first rollout.

## Judge Boundary

An LLM judge may provide diagnostic comments, but judge output is too variable
to serve as the release gate for this slice. Judge results must remain separate
from deterministic metrics.

## Threshold Question

The draft's 0.80 next-action threshold still required an explicit approval
decision. This review did not assign an owner or approve the threshold.

## Recommendation

Use deterministic metrics for release gating and keep judge feedback
diagnostic until a later review supplies reproducibility evidence.

metadata.content:
---
date: 2026-01-18
status: approved
authority: decision_record
---
# Data Retention — Final Policy Decision

## Decision

The approved current policy retains active records for 180 days and archived
records for 365 days. The policy distinguishes the two classes rather than
using one uniform period.

## Rejected Alternative

The uniform 90-day deletion proposal was rejected because it would remove audit
history too early and would not preserve the archive class.

## Legal Boundary

Deletion exceptions still require legal sign-off. The policy decision does not
authorize a deletion job to run before that sign-off.

## Approval

The compliance review group approved this policy on 2026-01-18.

metadata.title: 02-retention-review
metadata.content:

date: 2026-01-12
status: reviewed
authority: compliance_review
---
# Data Retention — Policy Review

## Review Finding

Uniform 90-day deletion would remove audit history too early and would not
distinguish active working records from archived records.

## Recommendation

The review recommended 180 days for active records and 365 days for archived
records. Deletion exceptions require a separate legal sign-off.

## Migration Constraint

Mapping and dry-run work may proceed, but no record deletion is authorized
until the legal sign-off and exception list are complete.

# Provider Selection — Final Decision

## Decision

The Atlas Lantern team selected Aster A as the approved model provider for the
synthetic pilot and its next integration slice. The selection is an approved
decision, while regional readiness actions remain tracked separately.

## Rejected Alternatives

Borealis B was rejected because the residency exception and additional
operational burden were not acceptable for this slice. Cedar C was rejected
because the review did not establish an auditable region commitment and its
streaming behavior did not meet the adapter requirement.

## Rationale

The decision prioritizes an auditable data boundary and an owned operational
path over the faster early prototype. The office-hours prototype observation
does not supersede this record.

## Approval

The decision was approved on 2026-01-22 by the Atlas Lantern technical review
group. Remaining readiness work must not be described as completed adoption.

# Provider Selection — Early Proposal

## Context

The Atlas Lantern team needed a hosted model for a synthetic document-review
pilot. The first comparison was made before the regional data boundary and
on-call ownership were written down.

## Candidate View

Borealis B was the early favorite because its prototype returned structured
JSON quickly and required little adapter code. This note records a proposal,
not an adoption decision.

## Open Questions

The team still needed evidence about data residency, operational ownership,
and the cost of keeping a fallback provider. The proposal was superseded by a
later comparison review.

metadata.title: 02-comparison-review
metadata.content:
---
date: 2026-01-15
status: reviewed
authority: technical_review
---
# Provider Comparison Review

## Comparison

The review compared Borealis B, Aster A, and Cedar C against the Atlas Lantern
pilot requirements. Prototype response quality was not treated as sufficient
for adoption.

## Data Residency

Aster A documented processing in the synthetic `eu-north` region used by the
pilot. Borealis B required a residency exception, and Cedar C did not provide
an auditable region commitment in the review packet.

## Operations

Aster A had a named operational escalation path and a bounded usage report.
Borealis B would have required the small team to own an additional failover
runbook. Cedar C lacked the streaming behavior required by the adapter.

## Recommendation

The review recommended Aster A for the pilot, subject to regional evidence and
an on-call runbook. Borealis B and Cedar C remained comparison candidates until
the approval record was written.

the approval record was written.

status: approved

---
# Retrieval Upgrade — Final Decision

## Decision

The team approved a phased hybrid retrieval path: retain BM25 as the lexical
baseline and add semantic retrieval behind the measured rollout boundary.

## Rejected Alternative

Replacing BM25 with pure semantic retrieval was rejected for the first release.
The benchmark showed lower recall on the reviewed sample and the team would
lose a useful exact-term diagnostic baseline.

## Rollout Boundary

This decision approves the approach, not unrestricted rollout. Embedding cache
security and release-readiness actions remain open.

## Approval

The retrieval review group approved this decision on 2026-02-14. A later status
update is authoritative for action completion.

metadata.content:

date: 2026-02-03
status: superseded
authority: working_draft
---
# Retrieval Upgrade — Semantic Draft

## Problem

Exact-term queries were missing a few paraphrases in the Atlas Lantern search
sample. The draft proposed replacing the existing BM25 baseline with a pure
semantic index.

## Proposed Change

The draft proposed removing BM25 from the first release and routing every query
through embeddings. It treated the early synonym-query prototype as evidence
that the lexical path was no longer needed.

## Open Risks

The draft had not measured cache isolation or whether exact-term diagnostics
would remain available. It was superseded after the benchmark review.

## Supersession

The February 3 pure-semantic proposal was superseded by the February 14
approved phased-hybrid decision. It is retained only as historical proposal
evidence and is not the current retrieval policy.

metadata.title: 02-benchmark-review
metadata.content:
---
date: 2026-02-10
status: reviewed
authority: benchmark_review
---
# Retrieval Upgrade — Benchmark Review

## Benchmark Scope

The synthetic benchmark compared the existing BM25 baseline, a pure semantic
replacement, and a phased hybrid design across exact terms and paraphrases.

## Results

The phased hybrid design reached 0.92 recall on the reviewed sample. Pure
semantic replacement reached 0.84, while the BM25 baseline remained useful for
exact-term diagnostics and reproducible failure analysis.

## Recommendation

The review recommended keeping BM25 as the lexical baseline and introducing
semantic retrieval in a phased hybrid path. The result does not authorize a
production release by itself.

## Risks

Embedding cache isolation and retention still required a security review. The
review did not claim that the cache action was complete.

# Retrieval Upgrade — Benchmark Review

## Benchmark Scope

The synthetic benchmark compared the existing BM25 baseline, a pure semantic
replacement, and a phased hybrid design across exact terms and paraphrases.

## Results

The phased hybrid design reached 0.92 recall on the reviewed sample. Pure
semantic replacement reached 0.84, while the BM25 baseline remained useful for
exact-term diagnostics and reproducible failure analysis.

## Recommendation

The review recommended keeping BM25 as the lexical baseline and introducing
semantic retrieval in a phased hybrid path. The result does not authorize a
production release by itself.

## Risks

Embedding cache isolation and retention still required a security review. The
review did not claim that the cache action was complete.

evidence validity can be checked against the frozen synthetic Gold records.
These metrics are reproducible enough to gate the first rollout.

## Judge Boundary

An LLM judge may provide diagnostic comments, but judge output is too variable
to serve as the release gate for this slice. Judge results must remain separate
from deterministic metrics.

## Threshold Question

The draft's 0.80 next-action threshold still required an explicit approval
decision. This review did not assign an owner or approve the threshold.

## Recommendation

Use deterministic metrics for release gating and keep judge feedback
diagnostic until a later review supplies reproducibility evidence.

metadata.content:
---
date: 2026-04-10
status: approved
authority: decision_record
---
# Internal Tool Integration — Final Decision

## Decision

The first integration slice will use the approved read-only connector and an
export bundle. The connector may read source records; the bundle carries
provenance for offline review.

## Rejected Alternative

The write-enabled direct API was rejected because it would cross the read-only
permission boundary and make source mutation available before human-confirmed
writeback exists.

## Future Boundary

Any source mutation remains outside this slice and must use the separately
reviewed human-in-the-loop writeback path. The decision does not authorize a
direct write demo.

## Approval

The integration review group approved this decision on 2026-04-10.

metadata.title: 02-security-review
metadata.content:
---
date: 2026-04-08
status: reviewed
authority: security_review
---
# Internal Tool Integration — Security Review

## Boundary Finding

A write-enabled direct API is not allowed in the first read-only integration
path because its permission and audit boundary is too broad for the slice.

## Approved Candidate

The review approved evaluating a read-only connector together with an export
bundle. Both paths must expose source references and retain an audit-friendly
checksum; neither path may mutate the source system.

## Remaining Review

The connector read permission was verified in the synthetic environment. Export
retention and checksum ownership remained open for the integration decision.

integration remains read-only connector plus export bundle.

## Follow-up

write owner or production operation was assigned here.

# Provider Selection — Final Decision

## Decision

The Atlas Lantern team selected Aster A as the approved model provider for the
synthetic pilot and its next integration slice. The selection is an approved
decision, while regional readiness actions remain tracked separately.

## Rejected Alternatives

Borealis B was rejected because the residency exception and additional
operational burden were not acceptable for this slice. Cedar C was rejected
because the review did not establish an auditable region commitment and its
streaming behavior did not meet the adapter requirement.

## Rationale

The decision prioritizes an auditable data boundary and an owned operational
path over the faster early prototype. The office-hours prototype observation
does not supersede this record.

## Approval

group. Remaining readiness work must not be described as completed adoption.

metadata.content:

date: 2026-01-15
status: reviewed
authority: technical_review
---
# Provider Comparison Review

## Comparison

The review compared Borealis B, Aster A, and Cedar C against the Atlas Lantern
pilot requirements. Prototype response quality was not treated as sufficient
for adoption.

## Data Residency

Aster A documented processing in the synthetic `eu-north` region used by the
pilot. Borealis B required a residency exception, and Cedar C did not provide
an auditable region commitment in the review packet.

## Operations

Aster A had a named operational escalation path and a bounded usage report.
Borealis B would have required the small team to own an additional failover
runbook. Cedar C lacked the streaming behavior required by the adapter.

## Recommendation

The review recommended Aster A for the pilot, subject to regional evidence and
an on-call runbook. Borealis B and Cedar C remained comparison candidates until
the approval record was written.

metadata.content:
---
date: 2026-02-14
status: approved
authority: decision_record
---
# Retrieval Upgrade — Final Decision

## Decision

The team approved a phased hybrid retrieval path: retain BM25 as the lexical
baseline and add semantic retrieval behind the measured rollout boundary.

## Rejected Alternative

Replacing BM25 with pure semantic retrieval was rejected for the first release.
The benchmark showed lower recall on the reviewed sample and the team would
lose a useful exact-term diagnostic baseline.

## Rollout Boundary

This decision approves the approach, not unrestricted rollout. Embedding cache
security and release-readiness actions remain open.

## Approval

The retrieval review group approved this decision on 2026-02-14. A later status
update is authoritative for action completion.

metadata.title: 01-semantic-draft
metadata.content:
---
date: 2026-02-03
status: superseded
authority: working_draft
---
# Retrieval Upgrade — Semantic Draft

## Problem

Exact-term queries were missing a few paraphrases in the Atlas Lantern search
sample. The draft proposed replacing the existing BM25 baseline with a pure
semantic index.

## Proposed Change

The draft proposed removing BM25 from the first release and routing every query
through embeddings. It treated the early synonym-query prototype as evidence
that the lexical path was no longer needed.

## Open Risks

The draft had not measured cache isolation or whether exact-term diagnostics
would remain available. It was superseded after the benchmark review.

## Supersession

The February 3 pure-semantic proposal was superseded by the February 14
approved phased-hybrid decision. It is retained only as historical proposal
evidence and is not the current retrieval policy.

hybrid pilot has not crossed the release boundary.

The owner and due date remain Yuan Li and 2026-02-28 from the action status.

metadata.title: 02-benchmark-review
metadata.content:
---
date: 2026-02-10
status: reviewed
authority: benchmark_review
---
# Retrieval Upgrade — Benchmark Review

## Benchmark Scope

The synthetic benchmark compared the existing BM25 baseline, a pure semantic
replacement, and a phased hybrid design across exact terms and paraphrases.

## Results

The phased hybrid design reached 0.92 recall on the reviewed sample. Pure
semantic replacement reached 0.84, while the BM25 baseline remained useful for
exact-term diagnostics and reproducible failure analysis.

## Recommendation

The review recommended keeping BM25 as the lexical baseline and introducing
semantic retrieval in a phased hybrid path. The result does not authorize a
production release by itself.

## Risks

Embedding cache isolation and retention still required a security review. The
review did not claim that the cache action was complete.

The synthetic benchmark compared the existing BM25 baseline, a pure semantic
replacement, and a phased hybrid design across exact terms and paraphrases.

## Results

The phased hybrid design reached 0.92 recall on the reviewed sample. Pure
semantic replacement reached 0.84, while the BM25 baseline remained useful for
exact-term diagnostics and reproducible failure analysis.

semantic retrieval in a phased hybrid path. The result does not authorize a
production release by itself.

review did not claim that the cache action was complete.

status: open

---
# Deployment Incident — Intake

## Impact

The Atlas Lantern synthetic service recorded 18 timeout/replay events during a
staging-to-canary exercise. A few action requests were observed twice; the
initial intake did not establish whether the provider or the replay path was
responsible.

## Initial Hypothesis

The first hypothesis was provider latency. It was recorded for investigation,
not as a confirmed root cause.

## Investigation Status

The incident review was still open on 2026-03-03. The root-cause review and
mitigation decision are later, more authoritative records.

metadata.title: 02-root-cause-review
metadata.content:
---
date: 2026-03-04
status: reviewed
authority: incident_review
---
# Deployment Incident — Root Cause Review

## Root Cause

The timeout recovery path replayed a request without carrying its idempotency
key. The replay therefore passed the duplicate guard as a new request and could
produce a duplicate action. Provider latency contributed to the timeout but
was not the primary root cause.

## Evidence

The review matched the duplicate actions to requests whose original attempt
had a key but whose recovery attempt did not. The trace comparison was completed
for the synthetic incident sample.

## Containment

The review recommended a bounded replay guard and end-to-end idempotency-key
propagation. Production verification was left to the status update.

metadata.title: 05-postmortem-draft
metadata.content:
---
date: 2026-03-03
status: superseded
authority: working_draft
---
# Deployment Incident — Postmortem Draft

## Draft Summary

The first postmortem draft used the phrase “mitigation complete” after a local
guard test. That phrase was a planning shorthand and was not verified against
the later staging, canary, and production status.

## Hypothesis

The draft attributed the incident mainly to provider timeout behavior. The
review later identified the missing idempotency key on replay as the primary
cause.

## Supersession

This draft was superseded by the root-cause review and the remediation status
update. It cannot establish production completion.

metadata.title: 03-mitigation-decision
metadata.content:
---
date: 2026-03-05
status: approved
authority: decision_record
---
# Deployment Incident — Mitigation Decision

## Decision

The team approved propagating an idempotency key through the timeout recovery
path and adding a bounded replay guard. This is the selected mitigation for the
synthetic service.

## Rejected Alternative

An active-active deployment was rejected for this incident slice. It would add
another route for duplicated side effects and operational coordination before
the idempotency defect was fixed.

## Verification Boundary

The decision record approves the mitigation design. It does not claim that the
production rollout or load-test verification is complete.

## Approval

The incident review group approved this mitigation on 2026-03-05.

metadata.title: 03-integration-decision
metadata.content:
---
date: 2026-04-10
status: approved
authority: decision_record
---
# Internal Tool Integration — Final Decision

## Decision

The first integration slice will use the approved read-only connector and an
export bundle. The connector may read source records; the bundle carries
provenance for offline review.

## Rejected Alternative

The write-enabled direct API was rejected because it would cross the read-only
permission boundary and make source mutation available before human-confirmed
writeback exists.

## Future Boundary

Any source mutation remains outside this slice and must use the separately
reviewed human-in-the-loop writeback path. The decision does not authorize a
direct write demo.

## Approval

The integration review group approved this decision on 2026-04-10.

metadata.title: 02-security-review
metadata.content:
---
date: 2026-04-08
status: reviewed
authority: security_review
---
# Internal Tool Integration — Security Review

## Boundary Finding

A write-enabled direct API is not allowed in the first read-only integration
path because its permission and audit boundary is too broad for the slice.

## Approved Candidate

The review approved evaluating a read-only connector together with an export
bundle. Both paths must expose source references and retain an audit-friendly
checksum; neither path may mutate the source system.

## Remaining Review

The connector read permission was verified in the synthetic environment. Export
retention and checksum ownership remained open for the integration decision.

metadata.title: 05-sandbox-demo
metadata.content:
---
date: 2026-04-16
status: informational
authority: discussion_note
---
# Internal Tool Integration — Sandbox Demonstration

## Observation

An isolated sandbox demonstration showed that the direct API could write a
sample record. The demonstration was used to expose the permission risk and
was not an approved integration path.

## Decision Boundary

No source record was changed by the synthetic review corpus. The approved
integration remains read-only connector plus export bundle.

## Follow-up

The group suggested documenting a human-confirmed writeback boundary later. No
write owner or production operation was assigned here.

metadata.title: 03-retention-decision
metadata.content:
---
date: 2026-01-18
status: approved
authority: decision_record
---
# Data Retention — Final Policy Decision

## Decision

The approved current policy retains active records for 180 days and archived
records for 365 days. The policy distinguishes the two classes rather than
using one uniform period.

## Rejected Alternative

The uniform 90-day deletion proposal was rejected because it would remove audit
history too early and would not preserve the archive class.

## Legal Boundary

Deletion exceptions still require legal sign-off. The policy decision does not
authorize a deletion job to run before that sign-off.

## Approval

The compliance review group approved this policy on 2026-01-18.

# Data Retention — 90-Day Draft

The first migration draft proposed deleting every record after 90 days. It was
intended to reduce storage and was written before the audit-history review.

## Assumptions

Uniform 90-day deletion would remove audit history too early and would not
distinguish active working records from archived records.

records. Deletion exceptions require a separate legal sign-off.

## Migration Constraint

Mapping and dry-run work may proceed, but no record deletion is authorized
until the legal sign-off and exception list are complete.

# Provider Selection — Final Decision

## Decision

The Atlas Lantern team selected Aster A as the approved model provider for the
synthetic pilot and its next integration slice. The selection is an approved
decision, while regional readiness actions remain tracked separately.

## Rejected Alternatives

Borealis B was rejected because the residency exception and additional
operational burden were not acceptable for this slice. Cedar C was rejected
because the review did not establish an auditable region commitment and its
streaming behavior did not meet the adapter requirement.

## Rationale

The decision prioritizes an auditable data boundary and an owned operational
path over the faster early prototype. The office-hours prototype observation
does not supersede this record.

## Approval

The decision was approved on 2026-01-22 by the Atlas Lantern technical review
group. Remaining readiness work must not be described as completed adoption.

# Provider Comparison Review

## Comparison

The review compared Borealis B, Aster A, and Cedar C against the Atlas Lantern
pilot requirements. Prototype response quality was not treated as sufficient
for adoption.

## Data Residency

Aster A documented processing in the synthetic `eu-north` region used by the
pilot. Borealis B required a residency exception, and Cedar C did not provide
an auditable region commitment in the review packet.

## Operations

Aster A had a named operational escalation path and a bounded usage report.
Borealis B would have required the small team to own an additional failover
runbook. Cedar C lacked the streaming behavior required by the adapter.

## Recommendation

The review recommended Aster A for the pilot, subject to regional evidence and
an on-call runbook. Borealis B and Cedar C remained comparison candidates until
the approval record was written.

status: approved
authority: decision_record
---
# Retrieval Upgrade — Final Decision

## Decision

The team approved a phased hybrid retrieval path: retain BM25 as the lexical
baseline and add semantic retrieval behind the measured rollout boundary.

## Rejected Alternative

Replacing BM25 with pure semantic retrieval was rejected for the first release.
The benchmark showed lower recall on the reviewed sample and the team would
lose a useful exact-term diagnostic baseline.

## Rollout Boundary

This decision approves the approach, not unrestricted rollout. Embedding cache
security and release-readiness actions remain open.

## Approval

The retrieval review group approved this decision on 2026-02-14. A later status
update is authoritative for action completion.

metadata.title: 01-semantic-draft
metadata.content:
---
date: 2026-02-03
status: superseded
authority: working_draft
---
# Retrieval Upgrade — Semantic Draft

## Problem

Exact-term queries were missing a few paraphrases in the Atlas Lantern search
sample. The draft proposed replacing the existing BM25 baseline with a pure
semantic index.

## Proposed Change

The draft proposed removing BM25 from the first release and routing every query
through embeddings. It treated the early synonym-query prototype as evidence
that the lexical path was no longer needed.

## Open Risks

The draft had not measured cache isolation or whether exact-term diagnostics
would remain available. It was superseded after the benchmark review.

## Supersession

The February 3 pure-semantic proposal was superseded by the February 14
approved phased-hybrid decision. It is retained only as historical proposal
evidence and is not the current retrieval policy.

metadata.title: 02-benchmark-review
metadata.content:
---
date: 2026-02-10
status: reviewed
authority: benchmark_review
---
# Retrieval Upgrade — Benchmark Review

## Benchmark Scope

The synthetic benchmark compared the existing BM25 baseline, a pure semantic
replacement, and a phased hybrid design across exact terms and paraphrases.

## Results

The phased hybrid design reached 0.92 recall on the reviewed sample. Pure
semantic replacement reached 0.84, while the BM25 baseline remained useful for
exact-term diagnostics and reproducible failure analysis.

## Recommendation

The review recommended keeping BM25 as the lexical baseline and introducing
semantic retrieval in a phased hybrid path. The result does not authorize a
production release by itself.

## Risks

Embedding cache isolation and retention still required a security review. The
review did not claim that the cache action was complete.

Replacing BM25 with pure semantic retrieval was rejected for the first release.
The benchmark showed lower recall on the reviewed sample and the team would
lose a useful exact-term diagnostic baseline.

## Rollout Boundary

This decision approves the approach, not unrestricted rollout. Embedding cache
security and release-readiness actions remain open.

## Approval

The retrieval review group approved this decision on 2026-02-14. A later status
update is authoritative for action completion.

metadata.content:
---
date: 2026-02-10
status: reviewed
authority: benchmark_review
---
# Retrieval Upgrade — Benchmark Review

## Benchmark Scope

The synthetic benchmark compared the existing BM25 baseline, a pure semantic
replacement, and a phased hybrid design across exact terms and paraphrases.

## Results

The phased hybrid design reached 0.92 recall on the reviewed sample. Pure
semantic replacement reached 0.84, while the BM25 baseline remained useful for
exact-term diagnostics and reproducible failure analysis.

## Recommendation

The review recommended keeping BM25 as the lexical baseline and introducing
semantic retrieval in a phased hybrid path. The result does not authorize a
production release by itself.

## Risks

Embedding cache isolation and retention still required a security review. The
review did not claim that the cache action was complete.

# Deployment Incident — Intake

## Impact

The Atlas Lantern synthetic service recorded 18 timeout/replay events during a
staging-to-canary exercise. A few action requests were observed twice; the
initial intake did not establish whether the provider or the replay path was
responsible.

## Initial Hypothesis

The first hypothesis was provider latency. It was recorded for investigation,
not as a confirmed root cause.

## Investigation Status

The incident review was still open on 2026-03-03. The root-cause review and
mitigation decision are later, more authoritative records.

metadata.title: 02-root-cause-review
metadata.content:
---
date: 2026-03-04
status: reviewed
authority: incident_review
---
# Deployment Incident — Root Cause Review

## Root Cause

The timeout recovery path replayed a request without carrying its idempotency
key. The replay therefore passed the duplicate guard as a new request and could
produce a duplicate action. Provider latency contributed to the timeout but
was not the primary root cause.

## Evidence

The review matched the duplicate actions to requests whose original attempt
had a key but whose recovery attempt did not. The trace comparison was completed
for the synthetic incident sample.

## Containment

The review recommended a bounded replay guard and end-to-end idempotency-key
propagation. Production verification was left to the status update.

metadata.content:

date: 2026-03-03
status: superseded
authority: working_draft
---
# Deployment Incident — Postmortem Draft

## Draft Summary

The first postmortem draft used the phrase “mitigation complete” after a local
guard test. That phrase was a planning shorthand and was not verified against
the later staging, canary, and production status.

## Hypothesis

The draft attributed the incident mainly to provider timeout behavior. The
review later identified the missing idempotency key on replay as the primary
cause.

## Supersession

This draft was superseded by the root-cause review and the remediation status
update. It cannot establish production completion.

metadata.title: 03-mitigation-decision
metadata.content:
---
date: 2026-03-05
status: approved
authority: decision_record
---
# Deployment Incident — Mitigation Decision

## Decision

The team approved propagating an idempotency key through the timeout recovery
path and adding a bounded replay guard. This is the selected mitigation for the
synthetic service.

## Rejected Alternative

An active-active deployment was rejected for this incident slice. It would add
another route for duplicated side effects and operational coordination before
the idempotency defect was fixed.

## Verification Boundary

The decision record approves the mitigation design. It does not claim that the
production rollout or load-test verification is complete.

## Approval

The incident review group approved this mitigation on 2026-03-05.

# Agent Evaluation — Rollout Decision

## Decision

The evaluation rollout will gate release on deterministic metrics for decision
accuracy, rejected-alternative accuracy, unresolved-item recall, and evidence
validity. LLM-judge output is diagnostic only and must not gate release.

## Scope

The first rollout covers the synthetic decision, rejection, unresolved-item,
and evidence cases. A multilingual slice is tracked separately and is not
silently treated as complete.

## Unapproved Threshold

The proposed 0.80 next-action threshold was not approved in this decision. It
requires a later sign-off before it can become a release rule.

## Approval

The evaluation group approved this boundary on 2026-03-21.

# Agent Evaluation — Metric Design Review

## Deterministic Metrics

Decision accuracy, rejected-alternative accuracy, unresolved-item recall, and
evidence validity can be checked against the frozen synthetic Gold records.
These metrics are reproducible enough to gate the first rollout.

## Judge Boundary

An LLM judge may provide diagnostic comments, but judge output is too variable
to serve as the release gate for this slice. Judge results must remain separate
from deterministic metrics.

## Threshold Question

The draft's 0.80 next-action threshold still required an explicit approval
decision. This review did not assign an owner or approve the threshold.

## Recommendation

Use deterministic metrics for release gating and keep judge feedback
diagnostic until a later review supplies reproducibility evidence.

# Internal Tool Integration — Security Review

## Boundary Finding

A write-enabled direct API is not allowed in the first read-only integration
path because its permission and audit boundary is too broad for the slice.

## Approved Candidate

The review approved evaluating a read-only connector together with an export
bundle. Both paths must expose source references and retain an audit-friendly
checksum; neither path may mutate the source system.

## Remaining Review

The connector read permission was verified in the synthetic environment. Export
retention and checksum ownership remained open for the integration decision.

metadata.title: 05-sandbox-demo
metadata.content:
---
date: 2026-04-16
status: informational
authority: discussion_note
---
# Internal Tool Integration — Sandbox Demonstration

## Observation

An isolated sandbox demonstration showed that the direct API could write a
sample record. The demonstration was used to expose the permission risk and
was not an approved integration path.

## Decision Boundary

No source record was changed by the synthetic review corpus. The approved
integration remains read-only connector plus export bundle.

## Follow-up

The group suggested documenting a human-confirmed writeback boundary later. No
write owner or production operation was assigned here.

metadata.title: 03-integration-decision
metadata.content:
---
date: 2026-04-10
status: approved
authority: decision_record
---
# Internal Tool Integration — Final Decision

## Decision

The first integration slice will use the approved read-only connector and an

metadata.title: 03-retention-decision
metadata.content:
---
date: 2026-01-18
status: approved
authority: decision_record
---
# Data Retention — Final Policy Decision

## Decision

The approved current policy retains active records for 180 days and archived
records for 365 days. The policy distinguishes the two classes rather than
using one uniform period.

## Rejected Alternative

The uniform 90-day deletion proposal was rejected because it would remove audit
history too early and would not preserve the archive class.

## Legal Boundary

Deletion exceptions still require legal sign-off. The policy decision does not
authorize a deletion job to run before that sign-off.

## Approval

The compliance review group approved this policy on 2026-01-18.

metadata.title: 02-retention-review
metadata.content:
---
date: 2026-01-12
status: reviewed
authority: compliance_review
---
# Data Retention — Policy Review

## Review Finding

Uniform 90-day deletion would remove audit history too early and would not
distinguish active working records from archived records.

## Recommendation

The review recommended 180 days for active records and 365 days for archived
records. Deletion exceptions require a separate legal sign-off.

## Migration Constraint

Mapping and dry-run work may proceed, but no record deletion is authorized
until the legal sign-off and exception list are complete.
